# Code of conduct

## The standard

Everyone taking part in this project, in issues, pull requests, reviews, and discussions, is expected to make it a place where people can do good work without being worn down.

That means:

- Assume the other person is trying to get something right, and read their work that way.
- Critique the change, not the person who wrote it. "This validator misses the partial case" lands; "this is sloppy work" does not.
- Accept that maintainers say no to things, and that a scoped project is allowed to stay scoped.
- Say what you mean. Directness is welcome. Contempt is not.
- When you're wrong, say so and move on. Nobody is keeping score.

Not acceptable, in any venue connected to this project:

- Harassment, intimidation, or sustained disruption.
- Sexualized language or imagery, and unwelcome sexual attention.
- Personal or political attacks, and demeaning comments about someone's identity or background.
- Publishing anyone's private information without their explicit permission.
- Any conduct that would reasonably be seen as unprofessional in a working relationship.

## Scope

This applies in every project space, including the repository, issues, pull requests, and discussions, and to anyone representing the project in a public setting.

## Reporting

Report unacceptable behavior privately through [GitHub's private reporting form](https://github.com/Clueless-Creations/b2c-app-builder/security/advisories/new), which is the private channel available on this repository. Do not open a public issue.

Reports are read by the maintainer. Your identity stays confidential to the extent GitHub's tooling allows.

## Enforcement

The maintainer may edit, hide, or delete contributions that break these rules, and will say why. Repeated or severe behavior leads to a temporary or permanent ban from the project's spaces.

If you disagree with an enforcement decision, say so in the same private channel. Enforcement here is one person's judgment, and it can be wrong.

## Attribution

Adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/), version 2.1, with the wording and reporting process rewritten for a single-maintainer project.
